LESSON: ARTICULATION OF LETTER SOUNDS

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.7: Articulation of Letter Sounds

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Articulation of Letter Sounds. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Articulate vowels correctly in and out of of the alphabet corresponding to each school upper case (capital)
2. Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher letter-sound provide opportunities correspondence in class articulating vowel sounds for learners to

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Articulate vowels correctly in and out of of the alphabet corresponding to each school upper case (capital)
   In simple words: practise until you can articulate vowels correctly in and out of of the alphabet corresponding to each school upper case (capital). Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. Demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher letter-sound provide opportunities correspondence in class articulating vowel sounds for learners to
   In simple words: practise until you can demonstrate awareness of letter sounds after the teacher letter-sound provide opportunities correspondence in class articulating vowel sounds for learners to. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Articulation of Letter Sounds using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Articulation of Letter Sounds in the examples.
2. Explain Articulation of Letter Sounds to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Articulation of Letter Sounds.
4. Show that you can: Articulate vowels correctly in and out of of the alphabet corresponding to each school upper case (capital)

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

2. Answer: Why is Articulation of Letter Sounds important for a PP1 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
